record.paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
record.original_question: If S/I is a Cohen-Macaulay integral domain, is its h-vector unimodal?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field and let $S = k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be the standard graded polynomial ring with $\deg x_i = 1$. Let $I \subset S$ be a homogeneous ideal such that the quotient $R = S/I$ is a Cohen–Macaulay integral domain of Krull dimension $d$. Choose a maximal homogeneous regular sequence $\theta_1,\dots,\theta_d$ of linear forms (after possibly extending $k$), and let $A = R/(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_d)$ be the corresponding Artinian reduction. The $h$-vector of $R$ is defined as
$$h(R) = (h_0, h_1, \dots, h_s), \qquad h_i = \dim_k A_i,$$
where $s$ is the largest index with $A_s \neq 0$. A finite sequence $(h_0,h_1,\dots,h_s)$ of non-negative integers is called unimodal if there exists an index $j$ with $h_0 \le h_1 \le \cdots \le h_j \ge h_{j+1} \ge \cdots \ge h_s$.

Question: Must the $h$-vector of every standard graded Cohen–Macaulay integral domain $R = S/I$ be unimodal?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture has been resolved negatively. In 2024, Conca, Singh, and Varbaro showed that the invariant ring of the special orthogonal group $\mathrm{SO}_t(K)$ acting on copies of its regular representation is a Cohen–Macaulay normal domain (even with rational singularities in characteristic 0 and F-regular in positive characteristic) whose $h$-vector is not unimodal, providing a counterexample.

status_evidence.title: Invariant rings of the special orthogonal group have nonunimodal h-vectors
status_evidence.snippet: For an infinite field K of characteristic other than two, considering the action of SO_t(K) on a polynomial ring via copies of the regular representation, the h-vector of the invariant ring need not be unimodal.
status_evidence.claim: Provides explicit Cohen-Macaulay normal domains whose h-vectors are not unimodal, disproving the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Invariant rings of the special orthogonal group have nonunimodal h-vectors (Journal of Algebra and Its Applications)
status_evidence.snippet: Published version showing invariant rings of SO_t are Cohen-Macaulay domains with nonunimodal h-vectors.
